fixes.explanation: Armies it is, friend. The kings "…came out with all their armies…" and they didn't send a few guys to check things out. Jabin, king of Hazor, sent word to other kings, and they came out with a multitude as numerous as the sand on the seashore (Joshua 11:1, 4). That's a LOT of people answering one message.

Treasures aren't on the list. The text says the kings came out with all their armies, along with a great number of horses and chariots. Hauling treasure to a battle would be like showing up to a big job with your best serving tray and no tools. I think these kings had fighting on their minds.

The Valley of Elah is a camp from a whole other story, where Saul, Israel's king, and the Israelites faced the Philistines (1 Samuel 17:2). This chapter puts the kings at the waters of Merom. Joshua 11:5 says they joined forces and encamped there. Different valley, same big battle energy.

The LORD doesn't say to hold off. He starts with "Do not be afraid of them…" and then says that by this time tomorrow He will deliver all of them slain before Israel (Joshua 11:6). That promise is about when He delivers them. Then Joshua and his army come upon the kings suddenly and attack (Joshua 11:7).
The LORD doesn't say to leave them there. His word to Joshua is to burn up their chariots (Joshua 11:6). And verse 9 says Joshua burned them up. Burning is the order, friend, not parking.

True. Verse 9 says Joshua treated them as the LORD had told him: he hamstrung their horses and burned up their chariots. That matches what the LORD told him in verse 6. Joshua carried out the order he was given.

Not even a little. Joshua 11:15 says he left "…nothing undone of all that the LORD had commanded Moses." Moses, Israel's leader before Joshua, passed the command along, and Joshua followed it. If I had that record, I'd frame it and hang it in the bakery.
The text says otherwise. Verse 18 says Joshua waged war against all these kings "…for a long period of time." So this wasn't wrapped up in a few days. The chapter covers a long stretch of fighting.

Gaza, Gath and Ashdod. Verse 22 says no Anakim were left in the land of the Israelites, "only in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod did any survive." Those three cities are where some of them did. Hang on to that list.

Those are the places where Joshua eliminated the Anakim, according to verse 21. He went after them in the hill country of Hebron, Debir and Anab. The survivors are named in verse 22: Gaza, Gath and Ashdod. So you've got the right region, just the cities from the other verse.
None of these three are named in this part of the story. Joshua 11:22 says the Anakim who survived were in Gaza, Gath and Ashdod. Those are the three to remember.

Inheritance, friend. Verse 23 says Joshua "…gave it as an inheritance to Israel according to the allotments to their tribes." It's the kind of thing handed down, the way a family keeps the good recipe. The land was given out by allotments to the tribes.
